channel.title: Daily Digest
channel.description: Curated tech blog summaries, inspired by Andrej Karpathy's reading list

item.title: Digitale autonomie: wat kunnen organisaties NU doen
item.description: Organizations are increasingly concerned about digital autonomy after years of dependency on American technology. Bert Hubert notes that regaining independence is a long-term challenge that requires acknowledging past outsourcing mistakes rather than seeking immediate quick fixes.

item.title: Magic the Gathering format: Fun 40
item.description: This article introduces 'Fun 40,' a custom Magic: The Gathering format designed for casual play. It outlines the specific deck-building constraints and gameplay philosophy intended to simplify the game experience.

item.title: Book Notes: “Poor Charlie’s Almanack”
item.description: This post summarizes key insights from 'Poor Charlie’s Almanack,' focusing on Charlie Munger's pragmatic approach to investing and life. It highlights his philosophy of seeking simple solutions, learning from mistakes, and prioritizing practical judgment over complex academic theories.

item.title: The stock market returns 4 %
item.description: This article challenges common optimistic stock market return assumptions, arguing that many figures ignore compounding, inflation, and hidden costs. It proposes a more conservative 4% annual return as a realistic baseline for long-term financial planning.

item.title: The $500 Price Increase
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: Plex has significantly increased the price of its lifetime subscription from $249.99 to $749.99. This move highlights the growing tension between the company's need for sustainable recurring revenue and its user base, which historically prefers self-hosting to avoid traditional SaaS models.

item.title: The Rise of Build-to-Rent Housing
item.description: The build-to-rent sector is experiencing a significant surge, characterized by the development of single-family homes designed exclusively for rental markets. This shift reflects evolving housing preferences and investment strategies within the current real estate landscape.

item.title: Read Cindy Cohn's new book, Privacy's Defender: My Thirty-Year Fight Against Digital Surveillance
item.description: This post recommends the book 'Privacy's Defender' by Electronic Frontier Foundation Executive Director Cindy Cohn. The memoir chronicles her career and covers three major legal battles against digital surveillance.

item.title: RFC: Artificial Contributors to Open Source
item.description: This Internet-Draft proposes a set of best practices for governing non-human, AI-driven contributions to open source projects. It mandates strict disclosure requirements, defines the responsibilities of human operators, and establishes standards to ensure code quality and accountability in an era of automated code generation.

item.title: Nobody is destined for greatness.
item.description: The article uses the story of Demosthenes, who initially failed as an orator, to argue that greatness is not an innate destiny but a result of persistent effort. It challenges the notion of predetermined success, highlighting how overcoming initial defeat is essential to achievement.

item.title: Couth and uncouth function pairs
item.description: This article discusses the mathematical concept of inverting non-invertible circular and hyperbolic functions. It explains how mathematicians restrict domains to create 'couth' function pairs, allowing for functional inversion.

item.title: Circular and hyperbolic functions differ by rotations
item.description: This article explains the mathematical relationship between circular and hyperbolic functions, showing they are linked by rotations in the complex plane. It illustrates this with the specific identity cosh(z) = cos(iz), demonstrating how multiplying by i represents a rotation.

item.title: The classic TreeView control lets me sort by name or by lParam, but why not both?
item.description: This post explains the technical limitation of the classic TreeView control regarding sorting. It suggests that developers must manually bridge the gap between sorting by name and sorting by lParam.

item.title: "No way to prevent this" say users of only package manager where this regularly happens
item.description: The article critiques the recurring issues and reliability problems associated with a specific package manager. It uses satire to highlight the frustration users feel regarding the software's persistent, preventable technical failures.

item.title: "No way to prevent this" say users of only language where this regularly happens
item.description: This blog post critiques programming language design flaws, specifically addressing how certain languages allow recurring, preventable errors. It highlights user frustration with languages that fail to implement safety features despite clear patterns of failure.

item.title: Whale Fall
item.description: This article explores the biological phenomenon of 'whale falls,' where deceased whales sink to the deep ocean floor. It reflects on the immense scale of these creatures and their final descent into the abyss.

item.title: Pluralistic: Shopping isn't politics (21 May 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow argues that 'voting with your wallet' is a futile and anti-progressive concept that inherently favors the wealthy. He asserts that this market-based approach undermines democratic processes and solidarity by reducing complex societal issues to mere consumer demand signals.

item.title: Alleged Kimwolf Botmaster ‘Dort’ Arrested, Charged in U.S. and Canada
item.description: Canadian authorities have arrested a 23-year-old Ottawa man suspected of creating and operating the Kimwolf IoT botnet. The suspect, previously identified by KrebsOnSecurity, is now facing criminal hacking charges in both Canada and the United States for orchestrating massive DDoS attacks and targeting individuals with doxing and swatting.

item.title: Datasette Agent
item.description: Simon Willison has released Datasette Agent, a new conversational AI assistant that allows users to query SQLite databases using natural language. The tool integrates with the LLM Python library and includes plugin support for features like generating data visualizations.

item.title: datasette-agent-sprites 0.1a0
item.description: Simon Willison has released version 0.1a0 of datasette-agent-sprites. This new Datasette plugin enables the execution of commands within a Fly Sprites sandbox environment.

item.title: datasette-agent-charts 0.1a2
item.description: Simon Willison has released version 0.1a2 of datasette-agent-charts. This update introduces "View SQL query" buttons beneath rendered charts to improve data transparency.

item.title: datasette-agent 0.1a3
item.description: Simon Willison has released version 0.1a3 of datasette-agent, an AI assistant for the Datasette platform. This update introduces "View SQL query" buttons, improved handling of truncated responses, and UI refinements for cleaner output.

item.title: Quoting SpaceX S-1
item.description: Simon Willison highlights a key disclosure from SpaceX's S-1 filing regarding their AI infrastructure. The document reveals that SpaceX is leasing compute capacity from its COLOSSUS clusters to Anthropic in a deal worth $1.25 billion per month.

item.title: datasette-agent-charts 0.1a1
item.description: Simon Willison has released version 0.1a1 of datasette-agent-charts, introducing enhanced color schemes for bar and waffle charts. The update also adds interactive tooltips, improves security by checking SQL execution permissions, and fixes specific charting bugs.

item.title: The famous o3 "GeoGuessr" prompt did not work
item.description: This article examines the limitations of the well-known 'GeoGuessr' AI prompt, noting that it often fails to produce the expected results in modern language models. It explores why certain prompting techniques that were once effective have become less reliable as AI architectures evolve.

item.title: The Fourth Era of Computing
item.description: The author argues that computing has entered a fourth era where raw, machine-readable interfaces like APIs and terminal commands are becoming easier to use than polished GUIs. As AI agents increasingly handle complex tasks, exposed system wiring is becoming more valuable than human-centered design for software.

item.title: What will better AI mean?
item.description: The article argues that the era of massive AI scaling is reaching diminishing returns, shifting the focus toward efficiency and taste. It suggests that AI development has reached a plateau where human-level evaluation becomes difficult, and the real challenge lies in determining what goals to optimize for.

item.title: Assumptions weaken properties
item.description: This article explores the logical relationship between system specifications and assumptions, demonstrating that adding assumptions inherently weakens a property. Through formal logic, the author explains why fewer assumptions lead to a more robust system that is guaranteed to function in a wider range of cases.

item.title: Square root of x² − 1
item.description: This article explores the mathematical complexities of defining the square root of a complex variable expression, specifically √(z² − 1). It highlights that while the process seems straightforward for real numbers, it becomes significantly more subtle and nuanced when extended to the complex plane.

item.title: Closer look at an identity
item.description: This article examines the mathematical constraints of a previously derived identity, specifically focusing on why the condition x > 1 and y > 1 is required. The author uses Mathematica to visualize the function, demonstrating that the identity holds only within these specified parameters.

item.title: What is the history of the ERROR_ARENA_TRASHED error code?
item.description: This post explains the historical origin of the Windows error code ERROR_ARENA_TRASHED. It clarifies that the code refers to the corruption of storage control blocks within memory management systems.

item.title: "No way to prevent this" say users of only language where this regularly happens
item.description: This blog post offers a satirical commentary on software engineering frustrations by highlighting a programming language where specific, recurring bugs are considered unavoidable. The author uses irony to critique the normalization of poor technical design and the resulting developer burnout.

item.title: [RSS Club] Let's meet up AFK
item.description: The author is inviting RSS subscribers to meet up for drinks or food during his upcoming Interrail trip across Europe. He highlights his positive experience meeting locals on previous journeys and encourages readers to get in touch if they are available to host or guide him.

item.title: How fast is 10 tokens per second really?
item.description: This post highlights an interactive web tool created by Mike Veerman that visualizes different LLM token generation speeds. It helps users intuitively understand what specific token-per-second rates actually look like in practice.

item.title: Google I/O, Gemini Spark, Antigravity
item.description: Simon Willison discusses the recent Google I/O announcements, expressing skepticism toward tools that are not yet generally available. He highlights the new 'Gemini Spark' AI agent and questions the role of 'Antigravity,' a mysterious component integrated into the platform's infrastructure.

item.title: llm-gemini 0.32
item.description: Simon Willison has released version 0.32 of the llm-gemini plugin, which adds support for the new Gemini 3.5 Flash model. The update includes notes on the model's performance and an example of an image generated using the upgraded plugin.

item.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash: more expensive, but Google plan to use it for everything
item.description: Google has launched Gemini 3.5 Flash, integrating it across its consumer apps, enterprise platforms, and developer tools. The update includes a notable price increase and introduces new features like the Interactions API, though it lacks the 'computer use' capability found in other models.

item.title: datasette-llm-accountant 0.1a4
item.description: Simon Willison released version 0.1a4 of the datasette-llm-accountant tool. This update specifically addresses a bug related to tracking response chains.

item.title: llm-gemini 0.32a0
item.description: Simon Willison has released version 0.32a0 of the llm-gemini plugin. This update introduces support for streaming reasoning tokens, requiring compatibility with the latest llm alpha version.

item.title: datasette-llm 0.1a8
item.description: Simon Willison has released datasette-llm version 0.1a8. This update specifically resolves a bug affecting the llm_prompt_context() hook, ensuring it correctly collects chains of responses.

item.title: Prompts are technical debt too
item.description: This article explores the concept of 'prompt debt,' arguing that hard-coded AI prompts in software systems can become difficult to maintain and evolve. It highlights the hidden long-term costs of treating prompts as static assets rather than evolving technical components.

item.title: Pythagorean Addition
item.description: This article introduces the alpha-max plus beta-min algorithm as a mental shortcut for estimating the Pythagorean theorem. By using a simple linear approximation, users can quickly calculate the hypotenuse without needing to perform complex square root operations.

item.title: Dumb Ways for an Open Source Project to Die
item.description: This article examines the common reasons why critical open-source projects become abandoned, including maintainer burnout, corporate restructuring, and academic neglect. It highlights how projects often persist in a state of 'ghost maintenance' without clear deprecation, posing significant risks for dependencies.

item.title: Approximating Markov’s equation
item.description: This post explores the mathematical derivation behind approximating Markov's equation, which involves integer solutions to x² + y² + z² = 3xyz. The author investigates Don Zagier’s transformation of this problem into the identity f(x) + f(y) = f(z) using the arccosh function.

item.title: Just shows that nobody cares about debugging the parity flag any more
item.description: This post highlights the ongoing neglect of the parity flag in modern software debugging. The author notes that this specific flag has been reported incorrectly since its inception, reflecting a broader lack of concern for legacy CPU features.

item.title: Book Review: Terrible Worlds: Destinations by Adrian Tchaikovsky ★★★★★
item.description: This review explores Adrian Tchaikovsky's collection 'Terrible Worlds: Destinations', praising its three thematically linked novellas. The author notes that while the stories ostensibly focus on space and time travel, they are fundamentally explorations of human loneliness.

item.title: Pluralistic: There's no such thing as "age verification" (19 May 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: The article critiques legislative attempts to mandate age verification online, arguing that such policies are fundamentally flawed and easily bypassed. It highlights the recurring pattern where politicians ignore expert warnings about unintended consequences, leading to increasingly invasive and ineffective regulatory measures.

item.title: Alternatives for the EDIT tool of LLM agents
item.description: The author proposes a token-efficient approach for LLM agent file editing by replacing the traditional 'check-and-set' method of repeating entire blocks of text with a lightweight tag-based system. By assigning short, checksum-based tags to lines, agents can perform edits reliably without the high token cost or hallucination risks associated with verbatim text reproduction.

item.title: The last six months in LLMs in five minutes
item.description: This post features annotated slides from a PyCon US 2026 lightning talk summarizing major LLM developments over the previous six months. It highlights the rapid pace of innovation and the significant industry inflection point that occurred in November 2025.

item.title: Wi-Wi Is Wireless Time Sync at 1 nanosecond
item.description: Jeff Geerling highlights Wi-Wi STAMP, an emerging wireless synchronization protocol developed by NICT. The technology utilizes the 900 MHz band to achieve remarkable nanosecond-level time synchronization and centimeter-level distance accuracy.

item.title: Weekly Update 504
item.description: This update discusses the ongoing debate regarding whether organizations should pay ransoms to hackers to prevent data leaks. Troy Hunt highlights recent examples, such as Grafana's refusal to pay, to illustrate the industry's evolving stance on this critical cybersecurity dilemma.

item.title: Travel notes: RubyKaigi Hakodate
item.description: The author recounts a three-week trip through Japan, detailing an extensive itinerary that included time with family, a conference, and a visit with a partner. The post shares personal travel notes, including activity suggestions, recommendations for vegetarian dining, and logistical experiences like riding the Shinkansen.

item.title: FediMeteo, HAProxy, and the art of not wasting snac threads
item.description: The author discusses the architectural evolution of FediMeteo, a lightweight weather service in the Fediverse. The article focuses on the challenges of maintaining efficiency and performance as the user base grows, specifically by optimizing backend request handling using snac and HAProxy.

item.title: Something’s Rotten in the State of macOS Icon Design
item.description: This article examines the decline in macOS icon design quality, arguing that Apple's strict adherence to a uniform 'squircle' shape is stifling creativity. The author suggests that Apple’s current design standards are regressing, forcing third-party developers to abandon unique, artistic expressions in favor of constrained aesthetics.

item.title: Human Bottlenecks
item.description: The article explores the limitations of AI in augmenting human capabilities, arguing that human bottlenecks remain a persistent constraint. It suggests that AI's potential is bounded by the inherent difficulties of scaling human cognition and decision-making processes.

item.title: How to be inspired without copying
item.description: This article explores the practice of copying masters as a legitimate method for creative growth. By examining J.S. Bach's study of Vivaldi, it argues that deep transcription is a powerful tool for learning structure and technique rather than simple plagiarism.

item.title: Always Be Blaming
item.description: The article explores advanced techniques for code comprehension by viewing code as an evolving historical artifact rather than a static object. By applying 'theory of mind,' developers can look beyond the code's current state to understand the author's original intentions and the historical context of its evolution.

item.title: Don't call yourself a Software Engineer, you are an AI Enabled Engineer.
item.description: The author argues that software engineers must rebrand themselves as 'AI-Enabled Engineers' to stay relevant as the industry rapidly integrates AI tools. They contend that while other departments quickly adopt AI branding, software engineers risk being left behind by sticking to traditional, outdated titles.

item.title: How I Use My Index 01 + Production Update
item.description: Eric Migicovsky provides a production update on the Index 01, noting minor delays but continued progress. The post also explores his personal workflow with the device and discusses the underlying product design philosophy.

item.title: CISA Admin Leaked AWS GovCloud Keys on Github
item.description: A CISA contractor inadvertently exposed highly privileged AWS GovCloud credentials and internal system configurations on a public GitHub repository. Security experts have labeled this one of the most severe government data leaks in recent history, revealing sensitive operational details.

item.title: Glaucous-winged Gull, Brown Pelican, Snowy Egret, Canada Goose
item.description: The author shares a collection of bird photography captured during a morning walk near the Los Angeles River. The post highlights local wildlife including gulls, pelicans, egrets, and geese observed while traveling for a conference.

item.title: The just-say-no engineer was a ZIRP phenomenon
item.description: This article explores how the 'just-say-no' engineering culture flourished during the era of Zero Interest Rate Policy (ZIRP). It examines how easy capital incentivized risk aversion and why that paradigm is shifting in the current economic climate.

item.title: The Tomy Tutor and the state of 1983 home computers
item.description: This article explores the history of the Tomy Tutor home computer through the discovery of original 1983 marketing documents. It examines the system's Japanese origins as the Pyuuta and provides historical context regarding the competitive home computer landscape of the early 1980s.

item.title: The Applicability of Spaced Repetition
item.description: This article explores the nuances of spaced repetition, distinguishing its effectiveness between factual and conceptual learning. It evaluates whether the technique is universally applicable or if different knowledge types require varied cognitive approaches.

item.title: GDS weighs in on the NHS's decision to retreat from Open Source
item.description: The article discusses the internal tensions within the UK Civil Service regarding the NHS's shift away from open-source software policies. It highlights how rare it is for such organizational disagreements to become public knowledge.

item.title: In the Empire's Defense
item.description: The author reflects on the morality of the Galactic Empire in Star Wars, questioning the binary nature of 'good' and 'bad' characters. By drawing parallels to real-world governance, the article explores the tension between maintaining order and the perceived chaos brought by dissenters.

item.title: GDS weighs in on the NHS's decision to retreat from Open Source
item.description: The NHS recently faced criticism for closing its open-source repositories following vulnerability disclosures. The UK Government Digital Service has now issued guidance advocating that public sector organizations maintain an 'open by default' policy to ensure transparency and security.

item.title: SQLAlchemy 2 In Practice - Chapter 8: SQLAlchemy and the Web
item.description: This final chapter of the SQLAlchemy 2 in Practice series explores integrating the SQLAlchemy ORM with Python web frameworks. It provides practical demonstrations of using SQLAlchemy within Flask and FastAPI applications.

item.title: The mistake of conflating intelligence and power
item.description: The article critiques common definitions of intelligence that equate the ability to achieve goals with high cognitive capacity. It argues that conflating intelligence with power leads to absurd conclusions, such as characterizing authoritarian figures as the most intelligent individuals.

item.title: Notes on pretraining parallelisms and failed training runs.
item.description: This article explores the technical nuances and common pitfalls involved in pretraining large-scale AI models. It highlights the challenges of managing parallelization strategies and analyzing the root causes of failed training experiments.

item.title: RLVR might be disproportionately bad at science
item.description: The article discusses the limitations of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) in scientific domains. It highlights that scientific theory verification can span centuries, noting that even established theories may occasionally produce flawed predictions.

item.title: Five Minutes of Prime Time
item.description: The author reminisces about their time at RSA, where a strong culture of intellectual curiosity and mathematics thrived among employees. This culture led to the author's participation in an HR-organized game challenge requiring employees to list prime numbers under a time constraint.

item.title: Reading List 05/16/26
item.description: This digest covers a diverse range of topics, including Tokyo's unique housing market dynamics and legislative developments regarding the Senate housing bill. It also touches on infrastructure security concerns and financial updates, specifically highlighting Fervo's recent IPO.

item.title: Make ZIP files smaller with ZIP Shrinker
item.description: Evan Hahn developed ZIP Shrinker, a browser-based tool that reduces ZIP file sizes by re-compressing contents using libdeflate and removing unnecessary metadata and directory entries. The tool supports standard ZIPs and ZIP-based formats like APK and EPUB, demonstrating significant storage savings through optimized compression techniques.

item.title: Pluralistic: Making sense of Trump's unscheduled sudden midair disassembly of the American empire (16 May 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow analyzes the perceived collapse of American hegemony, distinguishing between the ephemeral nature of political power and long-term durability. He draws parallels between current political trends and the historical decline of monarchies, suggesting that systems reliant on cults of personality and systemic decay are inherently unstable.

item.title: Warelay -> OpenClaw
item.description: Simon Willison uses a Python utility to analyze the Git history of a project called OpenClaw. The post documents the evolution of the project's name through its various iterations from its inception as 'Warelay'.

item.title: Quoting Julia Evans
item.description: Julia Evans shares her journey of shifting from viewing CSS as a source of frustration to embracing it as a sophisticated technology. By taking CSS seriously and deepening her understanding, she discovered that many perceived difficulties were actually solutions to complex layout challenges.

item.title: inaturalist-clumper 0.1
item.description: Simon Willison has released version 0.1 of inaturalist-clumper, a tool used to manage and publish iNaturalist sightings on his personal blog. The release follows several weeks of production testing and is designed to process and output observational data.

item.title: Western Gull, Rock Pigeon
item.description: Simon Willison shares photos of a Western Gull and a Rock Pigeon spotted during a morning bird walk in Los Angeles. The post offers a brief, personal look at local wildlife encounters near a conference event.

item.title: datasette-llm-limits 0.1a0
item.description: Simon Willison released datasette-llm-limits 0.1a0, a new plugin for Datasette that enables spending limits for LLM usage. It integrates with existing tools to provide per-user or global cost control based on configurable time windows and amounts.

item.title: How I use LLMs as a staff engineer in 2026
item.description: This article explores the practical workflows and strategies a staff-level engineer employs when integrating Large Language Models into their daily technical tasks. It highlights the evolving role of AI tools in high-level software architecture, decision-making, and productivity.

item.title: DeepSeek-V4-Flash means LLM steering is interesting again
item.description: This post explores the implications of DeepSeek-V4-Flash, focusing on how its architecture revitalizes techniques for LLM steering. It discusses the shifting landscape of model control and output optimization in the current AI ecosystem.

item.title: Eric Jang – Building AlphaGo from scratch
item.description: This article explores AlphaGo as a foundational model for understanding artificial intelligence. It highlights how the system effectively integrates search algorithms, experiential learning, and self-play mechanisms.

item.title: Language Registries Are Unstable by Default
item.description: This article highlights the inherent instability of language package registries like npm and pip, comparing them to Debian's 'unstable' branch. It argues that unlike traditional operating system package managers which offer stable release lanes, language ecosystems lack safety gates, exposing enterprise pipelines to unverified code updates.

item.title: Recovering the state of xorshift128
item.description: This article explores the technical process of reverse engineering the internal state of the xorshift128 random number generator. It follows the author's previous work on Mersenne Twister and lehmer64, providing a practical implementation and explanation of the recovery method.

item.title: The case of the Create­File­Mapping that always reported ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS
item.description: This post discusses a technical troubleshooting scenario where a CreateFileMapping call repeatedly returns an ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS error. The author humorously points out that the error occurs simply because the resource already exists, highlighting the importance of verifying existing object handles.

item.title: UK Government Kicks Out Palantir
item.description: The article explains that the UK government provides transparent access to public contract awards through their official portal. It encourages readers to verify sensationalist claims about government deals by checking the actual documentation rather than relying on misinformation.

item.title: Search engine results are truly terrible
item.description: The author evaluates the quality of modern search engines and AI tools by testing their performance against specific search queries. The results demonstrate that none of the tested platforms consistently provide high-quality information, often being misled by online spam and advertisements.

item.title: Pluralistic: No one wants a permanent gerontocracy (15 May 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow discusses widespread bipartisan support for implementing age and term limits across all branches of the US government. Citing polling data from G. Elliot Morris, the post highlights that a significant majority of Americans favor these structural changes regardless of their political affiliation.

item.title: Pluralistic: Kickstarting "The Reverse Centaur's Guide to Life After AI" (14 May 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow announces a Kickstarter campaign for his new book, 'The Reverse Centaur's Guide to Life After AI,' which critically examines the political economy of the current AI bubble. The author argues that the AI boom is a product of market saturation and investor-driven 'pump-and-dump' schemes rather than genuine technological necessity.

item.title: A few words on DS4
item.description: The author discusses the rapid rise of DwarfStar 4 (DS4), a project enabling efficient local AI inference on high-end hardware using asymmetric quantization. They highlight the shift toward using local models for serious, professional tasks and outline future plans to adapt DS4 to various specialized domains.

item.title: QR code generator
item.description: Simon Willison introduces a new browser-based tool for generating QR codes, specifically designed to handle both standard URLs and WiFi network configurations. The utility was developed with the assistance of Claude, showcasing the practical application of AI-assisted coding.

item.title: Not so locked in any more
item.description: The article discusses the shifting landscape of software development where programming languages and frameworks are becoming less of a permanent lock-in. With the rise of AI-assisted coding, companies can more easily migrate between technologies, such as moving from native mobile apps to React Native or switching between programming languages.

item.title: Quoting Mitchell Hashimoto
item.description: Mitchell Hashimoto observes that modern programming languages are becoming increasingly interchangeable, as demonstrated by Bun's rapid porting between Zig and Rust. He argues that languages are no longer a source of vendor lock-in but are instead expendable tools that developers can easily swap as needs evolve.

item.title: Managed agents are the new Lambda
item.description: The article argues that while cloud-hosted managed agents are powerful, relying on specific frontier labs creates significant vendor lock-in risks. It provides guidance on how to navigate these challenges and suggests alternative architectural approaches to maintain flexibility.

item.title: Welcoming the Bahamian Government to Have I Been Pwned
item.description: The Bahamas has become the 44th government to join the Have I Been Pwned (HIBP) free government service. The National Computer Incident Response Team (CIRT-BS) will now use the platform to monitor government domains for data breaches.

item.title: The First Democratic Tech Alliance Assembly
item.description: Bert Hubert reports on his attendance at the inaugural Democratic Tech Alliance assembly held at the European Parliament. The gathering featured a broad coalition of major European political groups, signaling a hopeful collaborative effort regarding technology policy.

item.title: The Biz Reaper
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: This article examines Byron Allen's acquisition of BuzzFeed, framing it as a strategic move by a businessman known for revitalizing distressed media assets. It explores the transition of leadership from Jonah Peretti and questions the future direction of the company under Allen's management.

item.title: Centrality is not vitality
item.description: The author argues that PageRank is often misused as a metric for measuring the importance of open source dependency graphs. By analyzing the fundamental differences between web link structures and package dependencies, the article highlights why PageRank fails to accurately reflect the actual vitality or criticality of software ecosystems.

item.title: Catch Flakes On Main
item.description: The article suggests maintaining a record of test failures on the main branch while using a merge queue to identify and eliminate flaky tests. By ensuring the main branch is always stable, developers can effectively isolate intermittent infrastructure or scheduling issues from genuine bugs.

item.title: A constant-space linear-time algorithm for deleting all but the 10 most recent files in a directory
item.description: This article discusses an efficient algorithm for cleaning up a directory by retaining only the ten most recent files. It emphasizes achieving this using constant space and linear time complexity through familiar data structures.
